name: GO Classes GATE CS | Computer Networks | Subnetting | Weekly Quiz 2

question.text:
Consider the IP address $132.239.15.87.$

Suppose that we were still using class-based addressing and the network administrator had decided to break the network into $16$ different subnets of equal size, What is the subnet address of the subnet to which this IP address would be attached?

  1. $255.255.240.0$
  2. $132.239.0.0$
  3. $132.239.15.0$
  4. $132.239.240.0$

Imagine a world where IP addresses are $8\; \text{(not} \;32)$ bits long. Suppose a router uses longest-prefix matching and has the following forwarding table:
$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|}
\hline \textbf{Dst IP prefix} & \textbf{Output link} \\
\hline 00 & 0 \\
01 & 1 \\
100 & 2 \\
\text{otherwise} & 3 \\
\hline
\end{array}
$$
What is the number of IP addresses reachable from Output link $3?$

A small university campus is assigned a large address block $12.1.0.0/17,$ but is only using a portion of these addresses $(\text{in}\; 12.1.1.0/24)$ to number its computers.

The university network is connected to interface $4$ of router $\text{R2,}$ Routing table of both routers are also given in the diagram.
Suppose the router $\mathrm{R} 1$ receives a packet with destination IP address $12.1.20.1.$ What path does this packet follow?

  1. $1 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 3 \rightarrow 4$
  2. $1 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 3 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 3 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 3 \rightarrow \ldots$
  3. $1 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 3 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 1$
  4. $1 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 1$

Which of the following IP addresses belongs to the subnet $137.132 .96 / 20?$

  1. $137.132 .96 .96$
  2. $137.132 .104 .104$
  3. $137.132 .112 .112$
  4. $137.132 .120 .120$

Consider the forwarding table of some router $\mathrm{R}$ as follows -
$$
\begin{array}{lc}
\quad \textbf{Prefix} & \quad \textbf{Outgoing Interface} \\
\hline 128.2 .0 .0 / 24 & \text{interface 1} \\
128.2 .1 .0 / 24 & \text{interface 2} \\
128.2 .2 .0 / 24 & \text{interface 2} \\
128.2 .3 .0 / 24 & \text{interface 3}
\end{array}$$
Suppose we perform route aggregation on the table (such that routing decisions are unchanged for incoming IP packets to $\mathrm{R})$ then what will be the number of rows after aggregation?

Suppose a router has built up the routing table shown in the following table. The router can deliver packets directly over interfaces $0$ and $1,$ or it can forward packets to routers $\text{R2, R3, or R4.}$ Assume the router does the longest prefix match.
$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}
\hline \textbf{Subnet Number} & \textbf{Subnet Mask} & \textbf{Next Hop} \\
\hline 128.96 .170 .0 & 255.255 .254 .0 & \text{Interface 0} \\
128.96 .168 .0 & 255.255 .254 .0 & \text{Interface 1} \\
128.96 .166 .0 & 255.255 .254 .0 & \text{R2} \\
128.96 .164 .0 & 255.255 .252 .0 & \text{R3} \\
\text{Default} & & \text{R4} \\
\hline
\end{array}
$$
Which next hop should the router use for a packet destined to $128.96 .167 .151?$

  1. $\text{Interface 0}$
  2. $\text{Interface 1}$
  3. $\text{R2}$
  4. $\text{R3}$

You are given the following network prefixes:
$$
\begin{aligned}
& 171.64 .121 .0 / 24 \\
& 171.64 .180 .0 / 24 \\
& 171.64 .18 .0 / 24 \\
& 171.64 .181 .0 / 24 \\
& 171.64 .19 .0 / 24 \\
& 171.64 .187 .0 / 24
\end{aligned}
$$
You are to aggregate the prefixes together into the smallest possible number of shorter prefixes such that you do not cover any extra IPs.
What is the smallest number of prefixes, and what are they?

  1. $1$ prefix; $171.64 .179 .0 / 21$
  2. $2$ prefixes; $171.64 .180 .0 / 20,171.64 .18 .0 / 21$
  3. $4$ prefixes; $171.64 .180 .0 / 23,171.64 .187 .0 / 24,171.64 .121 .0 / 24,171.64 .18 .0 / 23$
  4. $2$ prefixes; $171.64 .179 .0 / 22,171.64 .183 .0 / 24$

An Internet Service Provider (ISP) has the following chunk of CIDR-based IP addresses available with it$: 245.248.128.0/20.$
The ISP wants to give half of this chunk of addresses to Organization $\text{A},$ and a quarter to Organization $\text{B},$ while retaining the remaining with itself.

Which of the following is/are a valid allocation of addresses to $\text{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}?$

  1. $245.248 .128 .0 / 21$ and $245.248 .136 .0 / 22$
  2. $245.248 .136 .0 / 21$ and $245.248 .128 .0 / 22$
  3. $245.248 .128 .0 / 21$ and $245.248 .140 .0 / 22$
  4. $245.248 .136 .0 / 21$ and $245.248 .132 .0 / 22$

Consider three routers $\text{R1, R2, and R3}$ connected as follows


As shown in the diagram, $\text{R1}$ is connected to the subnet with the subnet id as $24.4.6.0,$ also $\text{R2}$ is connected to the subnet with the subnet id as $24.4.6.128.$

The netmask used in the network is $/26.$

What are the possible combinations of IP addresses of given interfaces $a,b,x,y,c,$ and $d?$

Consider each option as an independent option.

  1. $a: 24.4.6.1, b: 24.4.6.195, x: 24.4.6.250, y:24.4.6.200$
  2. $a: 24.4.6.1, b: 24.4.6.195, x: 24.4.6.200, y:24.4.6.68$
  3. $a: 24.4.6.5, x: 24.4.6.195, y: 24.4.6.250, d:24.4.6.200$
  4. $a: 24.4.6.1, b: 24.4.6.195, d: 24.4.6.250, y:24.4.6.200$

Pretend for a moment that IP addresses are $12$ bits instead of $32,$ and suppose you are allocated the block of addresses $\textsf{1011xxxxxxx}$ (i.e., all addresses that start with '$1011$' in binary notation). The network administrator has divided this network into $4$ subnets as follows:

  • Network $\text{A}$ uses prefix $/ 5$
  • Network $\text{B}$ uses prefix /6
  • Network $\text{C}$ uses prefix $/ 7$
  • Network $\text{D}$ uses prefix $/ 8$

After the subnetting, which of the following is true?

  1. There is only one unused block left of size $2^3$
  2. There is only one unused block left of size $2^4$
  3. There is only one unused block left of size $2^ 5$
  4. There is only one unused block left of size $2^ 6$

Consider two subnets connected to $\text{R1}$ as shown below.

The interface IPs are also shown in the given diagram.

Please note that for every subnet all-zeros address is reserved for the network name, and the all-ones address is reserved for broadcast. The network administrator wants to set up subnet masks so that the network prefix has maximal length.

What should be maximal length subnet masks for both subnets?

  1. $\text{Subnet1: 128.100.11.0/25 Subnet2: 128.100.10.0/28}$
  2. $\text{Subnet1: 128.100.11.0/25 Subnet2: 128.100.10.0/27}$
  3. $\text{Subnet1: 128.100.11.0/26 Subnet2: 128.100.10.0/27}$
  4. $\text{Subnet1: 128.100.11.0/24 Subnet2: 128.100.10.0/28}$

Which of the following is/are True?

  1. We can always do route aggregation irrespective of next hop is shared or not
  2. If a routing table contains prefixes $31.75/16\; ($for which packets are sent to port $1)$ and $31.75.93.128/25\; ($for which packets are sent to port $2)$ then an arriving packet with IP address $31.75.93.129$ will be sent to port $2.$
  3. A routing table can correctly contain the two prefixes $128.50 .128 / 17$ and $128.50 .128 / 18$ simultaneously.
  4. If a routing table is organized in order of increasing prefix length, then a routing decision may be performed by finding the last matching prefix.

Consider three hosts with a given IP address and subnet mask.

Which of the following is/are true?

  1. $\text{Host C}$ assumes that $\text{Host A}$ is in the same network
  2. $\text{Host A}$ assumes that $\text{Host B}$ is in the same network
  3. $\text{Host B}$ assumes that $\text{Host C}$ is in the same network
  4. $\text{Host B}$ assumes that $\text{Host A}$ is in the same network

Consider the forwarding table of some router $\mathrm{R}$ as follows -
$$ \begin{array}{lcl} \qquad \qquad \textbf{Prefix } & & \textbf{Outgoing Interface} \\ \hline \texttt{11010110 01100001 11111111 11000000} & & \text{Port b} \\ \texttt{11010110 01100001 11111111 10000000} & & \text{Port c} \\ \texttt{11010110 01100001 11111111 00000000} & & \text{Port b} \\ \texttt{11010110 01100001 11111110 00000000} & & \text{Port a} \end{array} $$
Suppose we perform route aggregation on the table (such that routing decisions are unchanged for incoming IP packets to $\text{R})$ then what will be the number of rows after aggregation?
